s001.text: UPSC, twenty twenty-four. General Studies Paper One, fifteen marks, two hundred and fifty words. Policies for social justice exist, yet the underprivileged do not get the full benefit. Comment. Here's the strange part. The official numbers say both things are true.

s002.text: Read what it asks. Comment means take a view, and back it. There are three jobs. Name the policies. Show why the benefit stalls. Then weigh it, with the Court's answer.

s003.text: Start with the frame. Articles fifteen and sixteen let the State make special provision. Article forty-six is the directive. Central posts carry fifteen, seven and a half, and twenty-seven per cent quotas.

s004.text: But in aggregate, the quotas are met. Scheduled Castes and Tribes met fifteen and seven and a half per cent in twenty twenty-four. Look at rank, though. In Group A, Scheduled Castes hold fourteen point two per cent. Scheduled Tribes hold six point five four.

s005.text: So the gap is about stock and spread, not only the total. Backlog posts did not fall between twenty sixteen and twenty nineteen. And the Court's judges differ on creamy layer for Scheduled Castes and Tribes.

s006.text: But in twenty twenty-four, in Davinder Singh, seven judges answered part of this. By six to one, States may sub-classify Scheduled Castes. They need data showing inadequate representation. The question's gap now has a legal test.

s007.text: Now we write. Two hundred and fifty words, about eleven minutes. Open with the Articles and the quotas. Then say that records still show gaps.

s008.text: Section one gives the reasons, each with a source. Backlog. Rank. Creamy layer. Spread within groups. Education. Every point carries a figure or a case.

s009.text: Section two is the Court's answer. Sub-classification is allowed, but only on data. Article three thirty-five is no bar. Backlog drives filled over four point eight lakh posts since twenty sixteen.

s010.text: Close with a balanced verdict. Policy exists and aggregate quotas are met. But stock, spread and access lag. The way forward is data. That is the view the question asks for.

s011.text: Now the easy answer beside it. It says all backward people benefit equally. The Court records that they do not. It says Scheduled Castes and Tribes are below quota overall. The gap is by rank. It says creamy layer applies to them. The order is silent, and judges differ. And it names no case.

s012.text: Here is the payoff. The same frame answers its cousins. Twenty twenty-one asked about the Right to Equality. Twenty seventeen asked about the scope of Fundamental Rights. Learn the Articles once. The full story gets its own episode in our Polity series.
